message.content: The explanation is scientifically sound, but the prose needs tightening. “In practice” is a generic hinge; start the steak example directly and specify that the pan is fully preheated. “Plenty of heat” and “stay hot as long as” are vague—give one rough, defensible comparison, such as a thick cast-iron skillet weighing several times more than a thin aluminum pan of the same diameter. The steak example is concrete, yet “enough stored heat to keep the surface sizzling” implies more certainty than the draft supports; qualify it with contact time or batch size. The limitation is correctly stated, but the final “Also” sentence adds a second limitation—sluggish burner response—and weakens the requested single caveat. Either fold responsiveness into the limitation or cut it. Rhythm is monotonous: several medium-length declaratives in a row, especially the thermal-mass explanation. Vary sentence length and subordinate the definition so the key contrast lands. Avoid “different jobs” as a cute abstraction; name conduction versus heat capacity. The causal chain from density to thermal mass is clear, but “typical skillet” needs a size/thickness anchor.
